study: Styles et al. 2014 — EEF Vocabulary Enrichment Intervention Programme (VEIP/VEFP), Bolton (pupil-randomised efficacy trial)
eval_evidence: EEF-commissioned trial with independent evaluators = National Foundation for Educational Research (NFER — Styles, Stevens, Bradshaw, Clarkson); separate from the program developers.
developer_evidence: Training and ongoing support came from the development team: teachers 'had supervision and support from the development team and from a visiting educational psychologist'; the programme 'is closely managed by the developers' and training was 'delivered by the developers'.
cascade_evidence: Existing class teachers 'received training on all three elements' directly from the developers/development team and then delivered to pupils; no train-the-trainer intermediary between developers and the delivering teachers.
counterfactual_evidence: Pupil-randomised trial comparing the intervention to a 'business-as-usual' control group; control pupils received the normal Year 7 English curriculum.
coaching_evidence: Delivering teachers had 'regular supervision and support from an educational psychologist based at Bolton Local Authority' plus development-team support — periodic supervision/support rather than recurring in-class expert coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: The programme was 'delivered in place of schools' usual Year 7 English curriculum' (replaces, not adds to, regular instruction) — no extra student-facing minutes/tutoring beyond the substituted lessons.
maturity_evidence: 'the first formal evaluation of the Full Programme'; teachers were new to delivering VEFP and outcomes measured at the end of the ~5-month single implementation period.
